title: Identify a combinatorial statistic with FindStat
when: recognizing a statistic that you computed on permutations, Dyck paths, graphs or other combinatorial objects, from its values on a dozen of them
finding the known statistics that agree with a conjectured one on small objects
whenNot: proving anything: a match says the values agree on the objects you gave, and only a Lean proof settles a statement
fewer than a dozen objects, or values that are all equal: too many statistics agree
numbers that are not the values of a statistic on objects: a sequence goes to oeis_search

collection.description: FindStat's name for the kind of objects, such as Permutations, Dyck paths, Graphs

object.description: An object of the collection in FindStat's notation: a permutation as a list [2, 1, 3], a graph as its graph6 text

value.description: The value of the statistic on that object

data.description: Objects of the collection, each with the value computed on it

matches.description: The statistics whose values agree, by their St number

examples.title: the number of inversions, recognized on the permutations of 1, 2 and 3

matches.name: The number of inversions of a permutation.

examples.note: A real call gives more objects, and the site may answer with more statistics.

implementations.description: FindStat's statistic finder (a POST of the collection and the data to /StatisticFinder/) through the client of @seshat/models, one request at a time with a pause between two. The address and the pauses are settings of the host profile. Not run against the site: it is not reachable from the development environment, and the request and the answer are guesses from its documentation as remembered.

environment.site: www.findstat.org, or the address FINDSTAT_URL gives (a mirror)
